full_judgment:
8. Considered the submissions and materials on records. Let us first address whether the initial complaint as filed by the respondent No. 8 was barred by limitation in view of Rule 57, Schedule 2 of the PPR Rules, 2008 as, according to the decision cited by the learned advocate for the petitioner, if it is found that the said complaint was barred by limitation we might have to follow the decision of a Division Bench of this Court and hold that since the very complaint of the respondent No. 8 was barred by limitation, he does not have any case before this Court. It is true that the recommendation by the Tender Evaluation Committee in its Second meeting held on 4-1-2014 was the initial cause of action for the respondent No. 8. However, we do not find anything in the minutes of the said Second meeting of the Tender Evaluation Committee (Annexure-VII to the Affidavit of respondent No. 3) as to when the said recommendation to award the work order in favour of the petitioner was communicated to the respondent No. 8. The petitioner also did not mention a single word in the writ petition as to when the respondent No. 8 was in fact informed of the said decision of the Second meeting of the Tender Evaluation Committee. The Affidavit of respondent No. 3 is also silent in this regard. However, the admitted position is that the complaint by the respondent No. 8 was field on 19-1-2014. Since Schedule 2 read with Rule 57 of the PPR Rules, 2008 has specifically mentioned the words “তৎ বিষয়ে অবগত হইবারঃ” —meaning that the counting of seven days will be started from the date on which the aggrieved party is in fact informed and since we do not find anything on record as to when such information was communicated, we have no option but to rely on the statement of fact as mentioned in the impugned decision of the Review Panel that the Tender Evaluation Committee recommended in favour of the petitioner on 15-1-2014. This being so, the presumption will be that the communication of such recommendation to the respondent No. 8 was in fact made on 15-1-2014 and, accordingly, the respondent No. 8 came to know of the said decision of the Tender Evaluation Committee on that day. Thus, the complaint, being admittedly filed on 19-1-2014, appears to have been filed clearly within the period of limitation. Besides, the decision of this Court as cited by the petitioner involves different set of facts in that in the said case the point of limitation was initially raised by the other party and it was decided by the Review Panel on the information available before it. However, in this case, the petitioner never raised that issue before. Considering above, we find that the initial complaint as filed by respondent No. 8 was very much within the period of limitation as provided by Rule 57, Schedule 2 of the PPR Rules, 2008. 

 10. Relevant provisions of Rule 58 provide that the Review Panel has to be comprised of at least three members and one of them would be the Chairman. It further provides that the Review Panel shall have members from three categories of experts, namely one on law regarding procurement, one on technical matters and one on contract and dispute resolution etc. There is no dispute that the Review Panel No. 2 did have three members. However, the impugned decision does not say anything about the expertise of the respective members. We also do not know whether these three members of the Review Panel were experts on the said categories mentioned in the said Rule-58. We even do not know that they were not experts or any one of them was not expert on any category as mentioned in the said Rule. The petitioner also did not mention a single word in the wit petition as to which member does not fall within the three categories mentioned in Rule 58. Therefore, we have no option but to agree with the submissions put forward by Mr Khan that the respondents did not have the opportunity to controvert the allegations as regards the constitution of the Review Panel 2. This Court also is not in a position to determine this issue as none of the parties including the respondent No. 3 has given us any information about the expertise of the members of the Review Panel, Since it was the statutory responsibility of the CPTU to constitute Review Panel and it is apparent on record that a Review Panel comprising of three members has passed the impugned decision, again the presumption would be that the Review Panel-2 was formed in accordance with law. Therefore, the submission as regards the legality of the constitution of the said Review Panel falls apart.
